pr_title: ActiveRecord PostgreSQL adapter: parse quoted values in range output
pr_body:
### Summary

When formatting the bound values of range types, PostgreSQL quotes the value using double-quotes in certain conditions: if its formatted representation contains parentheses, commas, double quotes, backslashes or whitespace (manual section 8.17.5, 8.16.6).

In particular this affects timestamps, which include whitespace and so will be formatted with double-quotes, for example `["2018-01-01 00:00:00",)`.

However, the parser for range values in `ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQL::OID::Range#cast_value` doesn't check for or extract quoted values. This results in a string potentially containing nested quotes being passed to the parser for the subtype.

In the case of timestamp ranges (where the subtype is `OID::DateTime`), this causes two problems:
 * The special-case handling for BCE in `DateTime#cast_value` is bypassed, resulting in incorrect positive instead of negative year values (Issue #37647).
 * `ActiveModel::Type::DateTime`'s `fast_string_to_time` parser can't be used and falls back to the `fallback_string_to_time` parser using `Date._parse`.

This change updates `Range#extract_bounds` to extract nested quoted values.

Fixes #37647

Well, this is awkward:
```
Error:
PostgresqlRangeTest#test_custom_range_value_escaping:
ActiveRecord::StatementInvalid: PG::InvalidTextRepresentation: ERROR:  malformed range literal: "[ca\t,do"g)"
```

Because Rails doesn't do any escaping when serializing bound values, including a bound value which requires escaping fails.

Should this problem be addressed as a separate issue/PR? As it stands, this PR fixes the more common case of receiving ranges with quoted timestamps from Postgres and failing to properly unquote them before passing the bound value to `OID::DateTime`.

issue_context.title: ActiveRecord fails to parse BCE (negative) dates in PostgreSQL time ranges
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Executable test case:
https://gist.github.com/chrisandreae/cfac1fe1e2e2b2b987e3aa826f803c86

* Create an ActiveRecord model for a table with a `tsrange` column
* Create and persist a record with a time range including a BCE (negative) year.
  `m = Model.create(period: (::DateTime.new(-1000, 1, 1, 0, 0) .. Time.now.utc))`
* Reload the model and observe that the `begin` of the loaded range has been changed to a positive date:
  `> model.reload.period.begin`
  `=> 1001-01-01 00:00:00 UTC`

This is caused by missing handling for nested quoting of range values in `ActiveRecord::ConnectionAdapters::PostgreSQL::OID::Range`.

### Expected behavior
The tsrange attribute should be reloaded with the same `DateTime` values as when persisted.

### Actual behavior
The tsrange attribute is reloaded with the absolute value of the year stored in
the database: for example, the year `-1000` is persisted as `1001 BC`, and so loaded as
`1001`.

### System configuration
**Rails version**:
`master` as of 803c6ba

**Ruby version**:
ruby 2.5.5p157

review_comments: Is it possible to find the cause why the assertion is passed even if actually `string_range` is not inserted?

Figured it out. This test suite's `setup` block silently `skip`s the test case if there is a `StatementInvalid` exception during creating the table and types. Because at that point I had not yet fixed the `teardown` to include `DROP TYPE IF EXISTS stringrange`, this exception handler was hit on subsequent tests with a `#PG::DuplicateObject: ERROR:  type "stringrange" already exists`, and so after the first test, the rest of the whole test suite was being skipped.

Fortunately I had already fixed this error, so the current branch actually runs the tests.
Is this part still necessary? Regardless of unquoting the quoted characters or not, that doesn't work for now.

Well, it's strictly still part of Postgres' output spec, so it seems wrong to leave it out of the parser just because Rails doesn't yet have the corresponding serialization side.

It also does work, for deserialization from Postgres: if there's a string range value `"ca\"t"..."do\\g"` in the database, Postgres will output that as `["ca""t","do\\g")` and Rails will correctly parse that with this code.

It's just that without the code that we split off into #39585, Rails is still lacking a way to perform the other direction and send such a value _to_ Postgres.

Basically Active Record doesn't fully support custom type.
If you'd like to leave it for custom type, at least I'd not prefer untested change (i.e. all behavior change should be covered by tests).

I think the problem is that this escaping handling is not specifically for custom types: it's about meeting Postgres' [specification for ranges](https://www.postgresql.org/docs/12/rangetypes.html#RANGETYPES-IO). Their documentation is clear on the cases where Postgres escapes the output and requires escaping on the input. It's actually only a coincidence that the formatting for the default range types happens to only include whitespace (and so not require input escaping).

I am happy to write a specific test that exercises this behavior. But the test for it will have to be a bit awkward, because we have chosen to hold back for now from correctly _serializing_ range values: it will have to only test the parsing. For the test to be nicer, we would have to reintroduce correcting the serialization to the PR.
Done: I've written a test for the parsing behavior.
